answer: Each new identity must escrow 14.8 POA and post three slack-water hashes from one licensed knoll tide station, timestamped by that station's crystal clock and accepted only inside the 7-minute stand of tide. Auditors recompute the hashes from the public gauge feed. A second signup on the same knoll, a hash taken outside slack water, or crystal drift beyond 2 seconds burns the escrow and locks the key for 15 epochs. Forging 1,000 aliases would require 1,000 unshared knoll stations and 3,000 on-time slack-water proofs; a reused gauge chain voids every linked identity.
